intro: Our field platforms connect coastal aquifers, riverbeds and the campus subsurface. Custom sampling and shared laboratory analysis link these observations with modelling and satellite data.

sections.title: Monitoring & modelling sites
sections.description: Three complementary settings for investigating groundwater exchange and subsurface processes.

items.title: Guanghai Bay sandy beach
items.image_alt: Groundwater field equipment and monitoring wells on the sandy beach at Guanghai Bay
items.summary: An intertidal field site for studying tidal forcing, groundwater exchange and coastal biogeochemistry. Multi-level sampling supports observations of vertical groundwater chemistry and its changes through time.
items.caption: Field monitoring at Guanghai Bay.

items.title: Huanghuadong River
items.image_alt: Huanghuadong River topography and monitoring wells in the river channel and sandbar, with the sampling layout and legend
items.summary: Monitoring wells in the river channel and adjacent sandbar provide depth-resolved observations of groundwater–river exchange. The site supports investigation of hyporheic flow paths and associated biogeochemical processes.
items.caption: River-channel and sandbar monitoring layout.

items.title: Campus groundwater modelling system
items.image_alt: Three-dimensional geological model of the HKUST(GZ) campus with boreholes and aquifer-layer legend
items.summary: Borehole and water-level records support a three-dimensional geological model and groundwater-flow modelling at HKUST(GZ). This work provides the foundation for campus hydrogeological assessment and development of a groundwater digital twin.
items.caption: Campus geological model and subsurface layers.

sections.source_note: Site photographs and figures: LogScience Lab research presentations.

sections.title: Groundwater sampling technology
sections.description: A group-developed system for repeated, depth-resolved groundwater sampling.

items.title: Multi-level groundwater sampling system
items.kicker: Developed by Yi LIU and Cheng XING
items.image_alt: Multi-level groundwater sampler showing the complete sampling tube and enlarged inlet, outlet and tubing-channel components
items.summary: The modular system collects groundwater from multiple depths within a single PVC monitoring well. Separate sampling lines allow repeated observations at fixed levels, helping resolve vertical heterogeneity in groundwater chemistry.
paragraphs: The design can be adapted to standard PVC casing sizes and has been used for high-resolution monitoring at Guanghai Bay. Repeated sampling supports comparisons across high and low tides, spring–neap cycles and wet and dry seasons.

items.title: Measuring oxalate-extractable iron
items.kicker: Published method · Yan ZHANG & Yi LIU
items.image_alt: Published flowchart for sample analysis and calibration of the 1,10-phenanthroline method for oxalate-extractable iron
items.summary: Oxalate can interfere with iron–1,10-phenanthroline complex formation. Yan ZHANG and Yi LIU developed a pH-adjustment approach that reduces this interference, enabling colorimetric measurement of oxalate-extractable iron for sediment and mineral studies.
items.caption: Analytical workflow reproduced from Zhang & Liu (2025), Figure 2.
